cases.name: Minimal Harness Scaffold
cases.prompt: I want to scaffold a standard-library-only Python harness into a fresh project. What files land where, and what command do I run?
cases.expected_output: Run scaffold_harness.py --target <project>. Governance files (AGENTS.md, feature_list.json, progress.md, session-handoff.md, init.sh, init.ps1, feature-list.schema.json) land at the project root; harness.py, context_manager.py, tool_registry.py, persistence.py, hooks.py, subagent.py, prompt_assembly.py land in <project>/harness/.
expectations: Names the scaffold script path under skills/scripts/
Distinguishes governance (root) from code modules (harness/)
Lists all seven Python modules
Mentions zero-dependency standard-library constraint
Mentions --agent-file CLAUDE.md or --governance-only as relevant options

cases.name: Session Continuity Across Restart
cases.prompt: A session crashes mid-feature. How does the harness make sure the next run resumes from where the previous one stopped?
cases.expected_output: Append-only JSONL persistence with immediate flush; replay reconstructs the message list and iteration counter. progress.md and session-handoff.md provide the cross-session restart contract.
expectations: Explains append-only JSONL with f.flush() on every event
Notes that replay reconstructs context, not side effects
Mentions progress.md as cross-session memory
Mentions session-handoff.md as the next-session restart contract
Distinguishes intra-session log from inter-session Markdown

cases.name: Structural Assessment Score
cases.prompt: How do I audit and score an existing project's harness? What does the score mean?
cases.expected_output: validate_harness.py scores 25 structural checks across 5 subsystems (Instructions, State, Verification, Scope, Lifecycle). Output is text by default, --json for machine, --html for a self-contained report. The score is structural — it confirms coherence, not real agent effectiveness.
expectations: Names validate_harness.py and its --target / --json / --html / --min-score flags
Lists the five subsystems by name
Explains that score is structural, not effectiveness
Mentions the bottleneck subsystem concept
Recommends pairing the score with real before/after agent sessions

cases.name: Verification Workflow
cases.prompt: How does init.sh enforce that an agent cannot claim 'done' on a broken workspace?
cases.expected_output: init.sh runs with set -e (fail-fast), compiles the harness modules with python -m compileall, runs pytest or unittest if a tests/ directory exists. A non-zero exit code blocks the agent's Definition of Done.
expectations: Mentions set -e on POSIX and $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop' on Windows
Mentions compileall or py_compile for static check
Mentions pytest / unittest discover as test command
Notes that the Verification Evidence (command and output) must be pasted into progress.md
Notes that Definition of Done in AGENTS.md gates done state on init.sh success

cases.name: Memory Persistence Taxonomy
cases.prompt: What is the difference between context compaction, JSONL persistence, and progress.md?
cases.expected_output: Compaction reduces the current LLM call's token budget. JSONL persistence records every event for in-session replay. progress.md is human-curated cross-session memory written deliberately at end-of-session.
expectations: Distinguishes intra-call (compaction) vs intra-session (JSONL) vs inter-session (Markdown)
Explains 80% threshold for compaction
Notes that compaction must preserve the cache prefix
Notes that progress.md is not auto-written
References context-and-memory.md

cases.name: Tool Safety and Permission Gate
cases.prompt: How does the harness prevent a model that calls run_shell from accidentally running rm -rf /?
cases.expected_output: classify_command in tool_registry.py inspects the command string and returns READ_ONLY / WORKSPACE_WRITE / FULL_ACCESS. Destructive patterns (rm -rf, sudo, curl, wget, shutdown) escalate to FULL_ACCESS, which prompts the user interactively. Order matters: more dangerous patterns are checked first.
expectations: Names classify_command in tool_registry.py
Lists three permission levels
Notes the rm-inside-rm-rf ordering trap
Mentions interactive input() escalation
References tool-registry-and-safety.md

cases.name: Context Budget and Prefix Cache
cases.prompt: What rules keep prefix caching warm across iterations?
cases.expected_output: The system prompt is built once and only appended to. Project guidelines from CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md are appended after the base prompt, not inserted. Timestamps and per-run IDs stay out of the prompt. Compaction summaries go into a new system message after the original prefix, not into the prefix itself.
expectations: Explains the prefix-byte-identical invariant
Notes that timestamps in the prompt invalidate the cache
Notes the ancestor-walk rule and stopping at the workspace .git root
Notes that compaction never edits the prefix
References context-and-memory.md

cases.name: Multi-Agent Sub-Agent Fork
cases.prompt: When and how should I spawn a sub-agent inside this harness?
cases.expected_output: Use subagent.py's SubAgentRunner when a scoped sub-task needs an isolated registry and conversation. Build a new ToolRegistry by copying only the parent's allowed tools, omitting spawn_subagent so the child cannot recurse. Pass a tight system prompt naming the deliverable. Collect only the child's final summary.
expectations: Names SubAgentRunner
States the single-level fork invariant
Explains the Spawn-Restrict-Collect lifecycle
Notes that child writes its own JSONL log
References tool-registry-and-safety.md

cases.name: Lifecycle Bootstrap Stages
cases.prompt: How should the harness gradually grant capabilities at session start?
cases.expected_output: Four stages: Minimal (read-only, no hooks), Verification (run init.sh — refuse to advance if it fails), Workspace Write (allow WORKSPACE_WRITE shell, run tests), Trusted (enable hooks if workspace trusted, allow FULL_ACCESS with interactive approval, allow sub-agents).
expectations: Names the four stages in order
Notes that init.sh failure must block advancement
Mentions the all-or-nothing hook trust gate
Notes that most sessions never reach the trusted stage
References lifecycle-and-hooks.md

cases.name: Scripted Validation in CI
cases.prompt: How do I gate a CI job on the harness score?
cases.expected_output: Run python skills/scripts/validate_harness.py --target . --min-score 80 --json. Exit code is non-zero when overall score is below the threshold. For richer artifacts, follow up with run_benchmark.py --html to publish a report.
expectations: Names validate_harness.py with --min-score and --json
Explains the non-zero exit code behavior
Mentions run_benchmark.py --html for CI artifacts
Notes that the score is structural, not a real benchmark
Mentions pairing with real before/after agent sessions
